Surface Engineering of Magnetic Nanomaterials and Ionic Liquid-Based Systems for Protein Modulation, Drug Delivery, and Biomedical Applications

Abstract:

Nanotechnology has emerged as a powerful interdisciplinary field for addressing critical challenges in biomedicine, particularly in drug delivery, protein aggregation-related&nbspdisorders, and tissue regeneration. The present thesis focuses on the design, synthesis,characterization, and biological evaluation of multifunctional magnetic nanomaterials and ionic liquid-based nanocarriers with tailored surface architectures for biomedical applications. Emphasis has been placed on understanding nano-bio interactions, improving therapeutic efficacy, and developing biocompatible platforms for disease intervention. In the first part of the study, polydopamine-coated magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (Fe 3 O 4 @PDA) were synthesized and comprehensively characterized using TEM, FESEM, XRD, XPS, FTIR, and magnetic measurements. Since interactions with plasma proteins play a crucial role in determining the biological fate of nanoparticles, the interaction of
Fe 3 O 4 @PDA with human serum albumin was investigated using fluorescence spectroscopy, synchronous fluorescence spectroscopy, and circular dichroism spectroscopy. The results demonstrated strong nanoparticle-protein interactions without significant perturbation of the secondary structure of HSA. Furthermore, in vivo toxicity studies using Drosophila melanogaster larvae indicated negligible cytotoxicity and only minor genotoxic effects at elevated concentrations, highlighting the favorable biocompatibility of the nanomaterial. The second part of the thesis explored the anti-amyloid potential of Fe 3 O 4 @PDA nanoparticles against lysozyme fibrillogenesis, a model system for protein aggregation studies. Biophysical investigations employing Thioflavin-T
fluorescence, circular dichroism spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and molecular docking revealed that Fe 3 O 4 @PDA effectively suppresses &beta-sheet-rich amyloid
fibril formation through interactions with aggregation-prone regions of the protein. Importantly, in vivo studies demonstrated that the nanoparticles reduced aggregation-
associated oxidative stress and nuclear damage in Drosophila larvae. Furthermore, treatment significantly decreased amyloid deposition in transgenic A&beta42-expressing
Drosophila brains, establishing the potential of Fe 3 O 4 @PDA as a promising nanotherapeutic platform for combating protein aggregation-associated neurodegenerative
disorders. To further expand the scope of multifunctional nanocarriers, a bromocholine- functionalized Fe 3 O 4 @PDA magnetic nanoplatform was developed. The silica shell
provided structural stability and surface versatility, while the ionic liquid-derived bromocholine moiety generated a hydrophilic and biologically compatible nano-interface.

These nanocarriers exhibited efficient loading and sustained release of the hydrophobic anticancer drug quercetin. Detailed investigations involving spectroscopy, molecular docking, and esterase-like activity assays revealed stable interaction with HSA while preserving its structural and functional integrity. In addition to drug delivery capability, the nanocarriers demonstrated remarkable wound-healing activity in vivo, promoting rapid tissue repair and highlighting their potential as multifunctional therapeutic systems. Finally, a novel magnetic ionic liquid-based amphiphilic system, MIL-N 8 , was synthesized and evaluated as a self-assembling nanomicellar carrier for hydrophobic drug delivery. Structural characterization confirmed the successful synthesis and stability of the material, while confocal microscopy, TEM, and FESEM analyses demonstrated spontaneous micelle formation above the critical aggregation concentration. These nanomicelles efficiently
encapsulated quercetin and provided sustained drug release following diffusion-controlled kinetics. Biological evaluation in SW-480 colon cancer cells revealed substantially
enhanced anticancer activity of quercetin-loaded MIL-N 8 compared to free drug, accompanied by increased apoptosis, elevated intracellular ROS generation, and pronounced dose- and time-dependent cytotoxic effects. The results established MIL-N 8 as an efficient and low-toxicity nanocarrier capable of significantly improving the therapeutic
performance of hydrophobic anticancer agents. Overall, this thesis demonstrates that rational surface engineering of magnetic nanoparticles and ionic liquid-based
nanostructures can generate multifunctional platforms with excellent biocompatibility, controlled drug delivery capability, anti-amyloid activity, and therapeutic efficacy. The
findings provide valuable insights into nano-bio interactions and offer promising strategiesfor the development of next-generation nanomedicines targeting protein aggregation-
related diseases, cancer therapy, and tissue regeneration.
